subject: Literature
subcategory: The Art of the Short Story
title: Gabriel García Márquez and Latin American Tales
description: A 60-second lesson on Gabriel García Márquez and Latin American Tales.

hook.text: In a García Márquez story, an angel crashes into a muddy backyard and the villagers charge tourists to see him.

buildup.text: A Very Old Man with Enormous Wings treats the miraculous with bored indifference, creating deadpan magic realism.

discovery.text: García Márquez learned storytelling from his grandmother, who told supernatural tales with total conviction.

twist.text: His short stories were overshadowed by his novel One Hundred Years of Solitude, though many consider them superior.

climax.text: He proved that magical realism works best in the short form, where the impossible feels most concentrated.

punchline.text: His grandmother's bedtime stories became Nobel Prize literature.

quiz.question: Where did García Márquez's storytelling style originate?
options: He studied it at a university writing program
His grandmother told supernatural tales with total conviction
He was inspired by European surrealist painters
